page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dual Intel Xeon 8259CL processors operating at 3.1 GHz. The instance delivers 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 384 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware architecture features 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 vector instructions and VNNI extensions. Direct access to bare-metal hardware eliminates hypervisor overhead, allowing full control over system resources and virtualization capabilities.

Storage and networking resources include 3,600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage and a 100 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic and multi-core processor benchmarks place the m5dn.metal in the top performance quartile, showing notable strength in parallel execution tasks such as software compilation with Clang and PassMark encryption suites. Cached and uncached memory read bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate high throughput, supporting resource-dense enterprise applications.

Benchmark results show static web serving speeds reaching 48.44 GB/sec and Redis SET operations exceeding 77 million operations per second, confirming strong multi-core and memory subsystem efficiency. However, single-core execution metrics remain moderate, and CPU-based LLM token generation speeds are constrained compared to dedicated GPU accelerators.

The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with high network bandwidth provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for resource-heavy bare-metal deployments. The m5dn.metal instance is well-suited for high-throughput databases, caching layers, software build farms, web serving clusters, and containerized enterprise workloads requiring dedicated hardware allocation.

It includes 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The system architecture supports AVX-512 extensions and full hardware virtualization access. Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution, memory read bandwidth, software compilation speed, and high-throughput network serving, achieving over 77 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded tasks and LLM text generation perform moderately due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware, the integrated high-speed local storage and high network throughput deliver solid qualitative resource value for bare-metal workloads. It is suited for large databases, in-memory caching systems, software build environments, and enterprise web applications.
